summary.intent: Close out review findings on previously merged release-preview and spec-gap PRs (update PR #436), then fix a confirmed bug where the publish output classifier mislabeled outcomes by matching 'already published' text before checking success.
summary.outcome: PR #436 description was updated. A new branch fix/publish-classifier-success-first was created, with classify_cargo_output and classify_npm_publish_output now deciding success first and requiring whole-word npm conflict codes (E409, EPUBLISHCONFLICT). The fix has a changeset, passed its targeted tests, and was committed and pushed, and a trail link to #198 was attempted. Full-suite, clippy and fmt results are not shown in the transcript.

repo: Changes to published crates need a changeset in .changeset/; test-only PRs explicitly note 'no changeset'.
Pre-merge checks used locally are cargo test --offline, cargo clippy --offline --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt --all -- --check.
PRs are linked to Entire trails (`entire trail link <id> --repo --project --branch --base`), and PR descriptions reference trail URLs.
A workspace with artifact slots fails a local release with E239 before the E132 (no origin) check, so no-origin fixtures with artifacts should assert E239.
Test harness provides a `stderr_of` helper, and the release module has `build_matrix_report` and `release_artifact` helpers for tests.
Setting GIT_SSH_COMMAND=false is used to simulate an unreachable origin in end-to-end tests.
Work happens in a git worktree under .claude/worktrees/macos-15-runners, and git is invoked via /usr/bin/git.

code.finding: classify_cargo_output and classify_npm_publish_output previously checked for 'already exists', 'previously published' and a bare 'e409' substring before the exit status. A successful npm publish prints a 40-char shasum and bundle names that can contain 'e409', so a good publish could be classified AlreadyPublished. The fix decides success first and matches E409/EPUBLISHCONFLICT as whole words only on failure.

workflow: Chaining several steps in one Bash call (commit, push, trail link, PR lookup) is efficient but obscures which step failed; the full-suite, clippy and fmt checks were later split into separate calls.
Piping test output through grep/head/cut keeps output small but can hide failures outside the filtered patterns.

friction: The combined test+clippy+fmt command was re-run as three separate commands, suggesting the combined output was unclear or truncated.
The review finding asked for E132 in the no-origin test, but that was the wrong expectation for the fixture and had to be corrected to E239.
open_items: No CLI test asserts E132 for a workspace without artifacts and without origin; only the graph-level test covers it. Deferred to the typed-report work in trail #198.
The PR number for fix/publish-classifier-success-first was queried but not shown, so it is unknown whether a PR was opened.
The full-suite, clippy and fmt results for the classifier fix are not visible in the transcript.
